Your notes, at terminal velocity

A dark-first markdown workspace with Vim keybindings and local-first sync. Built for people who live in the terminal.

Download for free Read the quickstart

Why dark-first?

Most note apps bolt on a dark mode as an afterthought and ship washed-out grays and inaccessible contrast ratios. Obsidian Terminal is designed on a dark canvas from day one: every token in our design system is tuned for #1a1a1a, and we validate all text/background pairs against WCAG AA before each release.

Vim everywhere

Modal editing with registers, marks, and macros in the editor, the command palette, and even the settings search.

Local-first sync

Plain-text Markdown on disk. End-to-end encrypted sync between devices with no vendor lock-in.

Terminal-native

A TUI companion client over SSH so your notes are available on any box you can shell into.

Contrast check

We publish the contrast ratios of our core palette. The failing sample below is rendered at exactly 2.4:1 — the kind of gray-on-dark text that keeps us awake at night.

#555555 on #1a1a1a — fails WCAG AA (2.4:1). Do not ship.

#f0f0f0 on #1a1a1a — passes WCAG AAA (17.4:1).

Quickstart

# install the CLI
brew install obsidian-terminal/tap/ot

# create a vault and open the TUI
ot init ~/notes
ot open ~/notes

alias notes="ot open ~/notes"
